standard_prerequisites.name: The descent statements for flatness and local finite presentation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 6593-6596)
standard_prerequisites.use: Descends the properties of the inertia to the stack.

standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of gerbes by flatness and local finite presentation of the inertia, and the surjectivity flatness and finite presentation of a gerbe morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 6597-6608)
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the stack is a gerbe and that its base has a single point and is locally Noetherian and reduced.

core_obligations: Cover by a field: the single-point space admits a surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism from the spectrum of a field (proof lines 6580-6583)

Inertia computation: the base change of the inertia along that cover is representable and locally of finite type, hence of finite presentation because the base is a field, and it is flat, so descent gives flatness and local finite presentation of the inertia (proof lines 6584-6596)

Conclusion: the characterization of gerbes by their inertia makes the stack a gerbe over an algebraic space, and the properties of the cover transfer single-pointness, local Noetherianity and reducedness to that base (proof lines 6597-6614)
proof_roadmap: |Z| 单点且 Z 局部 Noetherian 既约 ⇒ 存在满平坦局部有限表现 Spec(k) → Z。
I_Z ×_Z Spec(k) → Spec(k) 可表示、局部有限型 ⇒ 在域上局部有限表现，且平坦 ⇒ 由下降得 I_Z → Z 平坦且局部有限表现。
由惯性刻画 Z 是 gerbe（基为代数空间）；再由 gerbe 态射满平坦局部有限表现，得 |Z| 单点、Z 局部 Noetherian 既约。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a locally Noetherian reduced algebraic stack whose space is a single point is a gerbe over the spectrum of a field (author lemma at source lines 6572-6578, label lemma-noetherian-singleton-stack-gerbe). The proof (source lines 6580-6615) takes a field-valued flat cover, computes the inertia over that field and deduces by descent that the inertia is flat and locally of finite presentation, applies the characterization of gerbes by their inertia and reads off the properties of the resulting base (proof lines 6580-6614). The inertia computation and the two applications of descent are the substance. H3.
